## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Āsavagocchaka, Kusalattika* constitutes section 3.4 of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh text of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. In this section, conditional relations are expounded across the matrices combining the *āsavagocchaka* (the cluster of dyads pertaining to the taints or cankers) and the *kusalattika* (the triad of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate dhammas).

According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shares an extensive degree of internal text reuse across the Abhidhamma, totaling 4,332 matching passages across 140 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignments occur with other combinatory sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, most notably *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 553 matches), *Hetugocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.2; 365 matches), *Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 2.3; 256 matches), *Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.13; 221 matches), and *Kusalattika, Āsavaparāmāsagocchaka* (Patthana 4.4; 185 matches) [DharmaNexus].
